_README: THE MONEY AND CALL RULES BOTH DASHBOARDS OBEY.
This file exists because the same question was being answered twice, in two
languages, in two repositories — and the two answers drifted apart four
separate times in a single evening (2026-08-18):
1. what counts as a sale       tracker said 'outcome typed on the day',
dashboard said 'money in Whop'
2. the deposit floor           tracker had $100, dashboard had $0
3. the same floor again        applied to Whop payments but not to money
typed into Collected On Call
4. what a payment proves       a payment was being read as proof that a
CALL HAD HAPPENED, not just that someone paid
Every one was found by a human noticing two screens disagreeing. That is not
a detection mechanism, it is luck.
TWO COPIES, ONE FILE. The Sales Command Center and the KPI dashboard deploy
independently, so each repository carries its own copy and neither can reach
the other at runtime. Copy this file WHOLE; never edit one side. Both repos
run `npm run check:rules`, which compares the two copies when they sit side
by side on a laptop and fails when they differ.
Changing a rule means: edit here, copy to the other repo, bump `version`,
run check:rules in both.

min_deposit.statement: A payment proves a sale once it reaches $100. Below that it is a token, and the deal stays whatever the closer recorded.
applies_to: money received through the payment processor
money taken during the call and typed into Collected On Call
min_deposit.why_flat_not_percentage: Under a percentage bar the same $500 deposit was a sale on a $2,000 deal and not one on a $4,000 deal, which judges the closer by the size of the offer rather than by what they actually banked.
min_deposit.source: [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-08-18] 'even if a deposit doesnt pay the rest, its still technically a close unless its under $100 i think then that we shouldnt count as a close.'
min_deposit.a_membership_signup_is_a_deal: A first payment for a membership counts as a deal closed on the same footing as a coaching sale, so a $499 sign-up sits in Deals closed beside a $5,000 deal. Renewals of a membership already bought are cash and never a new deal - see IS_RENEWAL in the KPI dashboard's lead-window.js - so the same person cannot be counted again each month.
min_deposit.why_no_second_floor: Asked because a $499 sign-up next to $4,000 coaching deals looks like a different kind of event. It is not: the same person can buy either, and a floor high enough to exclude the membership would also exclude every deposit the $100 rule exists to count. [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-09-05] 'yes a 499$ membership is still a deal.'

a_close_needs_money_to_have_moved.statement: A call is a close only when money actually moved. A price agreed with nothing collected is a FOLLOW-UP, not a sale — however the closer recorded the outcome.
a_close_needs_money_to_have_moved.source: [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-09-06] 'if it was never taken on the call then it wasnt a close, a close is only counted if cash was collected, if a price was agreed but no cash was collected then its simply a follow up'
what_counts_as_money_moving: a payment through the processor, dated on or after the call, at or above min_deposit
money taken during the call and typed into Collected On Call, at or above min_deposit
a_close_needs_money_to_have_moved.what_does_NOT_count: the outcome a closer typed. Until now 'closed' on the tracker was enough on its own, so a verbal commitment with nothing banked sat in revenue and in the close rate exactly like a paid deal.
a_close_needs_money_to_have_moved.the_deal_value_is_unchanged: Once money HAS moved the deal is still worth its agreed price, not the cash. A $6,000 plan with $500 paid is a $6,000 close with $5,500 outstanding. This rule decides WHETHER a call closed, never what it was worth - see deal_value. [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-09-06] 'yes agreed price stays'.
a_close_needs_money_to_have_moved.why_this_is_not_a_reversal: The 2026-08-18 rulings in min_deposit and deal_value both presuppose money moved - a deposit IS cash, and an instalment deal has a first payment. Neither covered a deal where nothing ever arrived, which is the case this settles.
a_close_needs_money_to_have_moved.measured_when_it_was_written: Brey, 2026-09-06: twelve deals across the account had never received a penny, worth $29,250 of recorded revenue. August close rate 57.4% -> 42.6% and revenue $78,758 -> $62,508; September 62.5% -> 50.0%. Each of the twelve was checked against Whop by name as well as by email first, in case the money had arrived under a different address. It had not.
a_close_needs_money_to_have_moved.the_call_that_produced_it: ABandZz, 5 September, recorded as a customer at $8,000. The recording has him agreeing a $200 deposit and asking to send it by Zelle after a trip to the bank; Christian's closing words are 'let me know when that 200 is ready'. Nothing ever arrived.

data_starts.statement: Nothing before 2026-08-16 is worth reconciling. The reconciliation reports ignore earlier rows; the dashboard still SHOWS the history.
data_starts.why: The tracking was built around this date - the inbox sync began recording conversations on the 16th and the booking form started asking for the Instagram handle on the 18th. Before that there is no route from a conversation to a booking to a payment, so a gap in an older row measures the absence of the system rather than anything anybody did. Chasing those rows is work that cannot come out right.
data_starts.what_it_does_NOT_do: It is not a floor on the dashboard. Revenue, close rate and every period still count the full history, because that money was really earned and really paid. This governs what the CHECKS report, so their lists stay actionable.
data_starts.known_gap: Bookings made on 16 and 17 August carry no Instagram handle - the question went onto the form on the 18th. Two days of bookings are therefore unjoinable to a conversation by design, not by fault.
data_starts.source: [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-08-24] 'i dont want u to focus on old old calls etc anymore we want to just focus on since we setup the calendar, no matter what we do that data from previous to that is tainted, we just can make sure only since we setup the dash the numbers are clean'

what_a_payment_proves.statement: A payment proves a SALE. It does not prove that a CALL HAPPENED.
what_a_payment_proves.why: Everyone who arrives by the payment route is by definition a buyer, so counting them as a call held puts them on both sides of the close rate and can only push it up. Measured 2026-08-18 on Brey's August: 59.0% against the tracker's 48.6%, and the spread was almost entirely this.
a_call_happened_when: someone recorded an outcome for it (closed, deposit, or no_close)
a call for that person exists on the tracker AND its own outcome is not 'no show'
not_evidence_a_call_happened: a Calendly booking whose time has passed - Calendly is authoritative that a booking was MADE, but with no-shows going unmarked, counting those as held would assume a 100% show rate

refund.name: REFUND
refund.statement: A refunded deal is removed from revenue, from cash collected, and from the close rate — out of BOTH sides of it, not counted as a loss. The closer did close them; the customer later left, and scoring it as a failed call would make a different claim from the one the refund actually makes, on the closer's record.
refund.source: [STATED - Moayad, chat 2026-08-18] 'should be removed from revenue and cash collected, should also be removed from close rate.'
refund.cash_needs_no_rule: The processor reports a refund against the original payment, so refunded money nets to zero before it is ever read as cash. Verified against Whop on 2026-08-18: Vellatino Crawford, final_amount 2000, refunded_amount 2000, read as 0.
refund.outranks_the_arithmetic: Checked explicitly rather than left to fall out of a status list: a partly-refunded buyer would otherwise be put back by the paid-enough test. A REFUND on the tracker is a statement about the deal and beats what is left of their payments.

deal_value.statement: A deal is worth its recorded price, and never less than the cash actually received.
deal_value.why: A follow-up that later paid often carries no price at all, so reading the recorded price alone books a paid deal at zero. Where a price IS recorded and only part has been paid, the recorded price still wins - that is the deal value, and the remainder is what is outstanding.

source_of_truth.statement: Every fact has exactly one owning system. A disagreement between two sources is not a vote — you go and ask the owner. Secondary sources fill a gap only when the answer is unambiguous.

owns.bookings_and_cancellations: Calendly — that a call was booked, moved or called off, by whom and with how much notice. It cannot say whether anybody turned up.
owns.money_received: Whop — how much arrived, when, and what was refunded. It cannot say what was agreed, and it cannot say a call happened.
owns.what_was_agreed: the recording — the price, the payment plan and the dates. The only record of the agreement itself.
owns.whether_anybody_turned_up: the recording — that it exists, and how much was said on it.
owns.how_a_call_went: the recording. The Notion tracker is a person's reading of it, not the source.
owns.who_took_the_call: Calendly's assignment, checked against who actually speaks on the recording.

own_nothing.the_closers_sheets: A claim by the person being measured. Never the deciding answer.
own_nothing.the_trackers_money_columns: Typed by hand. The tracker owns how a call went, never what was banked.
own_nothing.why_they_still_matter: They are alarms rather than answers. A closer's sheet ahead of the tracker means calls are not reaching the tracker; the tracker ahead of Whop means money was recorded that never arrived; Whop ahead of both means sales are happening on calls nobody logged.

source_of_truth.when_the_owner_cannot_answer: Say so and stop. Never drop quietly to a weaker source — that substitution is where the repeated arguments came from.
source_of_truth.cash_is_a_floor_not_the_deal: Whop owns money received, which is a FLOOR on the deal value and never the deal value. Measured 2026-09-05: Brian had $1,000 in Whop, his closer's sheet said $2,000, the tracker said $4,000, and the recording had him agreeing to $4,000 with $3,000 still owed. Letting the processor decide deal size writes off every unpaid instalment and shrinks every payment plan to whatever has been paid so far. See deal_value above, which this restates from the other direction.
source_of_truth.totals_agreeing_proves_nothing_per_row: September 2026: the two closer sheets came to $35,850 against Whop's $35,396, which reads as healthy. It hid $3,750 marked collected that never arrived and about the same again of real Whop money from August calls and subscription renewals. The gaps cancelled. Whenever the output is a list of PEOPLE, reconcile rows and not totals.
source_of_truth.source: [STATED — Moayad, chat 2026-09-05] asked for a fixed method after a third round of arguing the same figure from whichever source was nearest to hand.

cash_split.statement: Cash collected in a period splits four ways, by the call behind each payment: NEW - the call is a win that had not closed before the period; REMAINDER - the call is a win that closed before the period opened; DEPOSITS - the call is not a win; NO CALL - no call could be tied to the payment at all.
cash_split.why: One cash figure answers 'how much money arrived' and is read as 'how much did we sell'. In a business taking payment plans those are different questions: a month where nothing closed and every instalment landed looks identical to a month of new deals paid in full.
cash_split.the_four_sum_to_the_total: NO CALL is never counted. It is what is left of the processor's total once the other three are taken off it, so the breakdown adds up to the figure above it by construction rather than by two counts happening to agree.
cash_split.deposits_are_not_win_only: A deposit taken while booking a follow-up is money that moved and is already inside the cash total. Counting only wins would leave it in the total and outside every bucket, where it would read as money with no call behind it.
cash_split.a_payment_that_arrives_before_its_call: Counted as NEW. REMAINDER means one thing only - the deal closed before this period opened - so a deal that closes later in the same period, or just after it, is this period's selling and not an older deal paying off.
cash_split.an_all_time_window_has_no_remainder: With no start date there is no 'before', so every payment belongs to the deal it was made against.
cash_split.refuses_rather_than_guesses: If the three attributed figures exceed the processor's total, something has been counted twice and every figure is wrong in a way that still adds up on screen. The split is withheld entirely; the total shows on its own.
cash_split.source: [Plan 2026-09-04, sales-command-center/docs/plan-2026-09-tracker-upgrades.md] Taken from the Airtable tracker audited in reference/sales-tracker-benchmarks, which separates new cash from remainder cash and from deposits.
